answer: A practical defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: each agent must lock a small refundable stake and accumulate attested work over time before it can earn rewards. New identities start with narrow rate limits, and peers randomly audit completed tasks, so flooding the network with clones costs more than it gains. Think of reputation as a walnut that only opens after sustained effort, not as an umber stamp anyone can print across the tundra of anonymous accounts; without a history, a newcomer simply cannot claim the same trust.
